question: A triangle has an area of 45 cm² and a base of 15 cm. What is its height?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of a triangle = (2 × Area) ÷ Base

Height = (2 × 45) ÷ 15

Height = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the triangle = 45 cm²

Base of the triangle = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e71497fbe89dedde2651646ccf59b3298cd408fbdd6eb41f3a7bf56a632b69a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 45 = 1/2 × 15 × Height

⇒ 45 × 2 = 15 × Height

⇒ 90 = 15 × Height

⇒ Height = 90 ÷ 15

⇒ Height = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used when all three sides (a, b, c) are known: Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a+b+c)/2.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For a triangle with all equal sides 'a', Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a².

Right-Angled Triangle

The height is simply the perpendicular side, making the calculation Area = 1/2 × base × perpendicular.</p
